name: Prize crossword No 27,196
preamble: Eight solutions are of a kind, not further defined.

clue.text: Put out a horse adjudged to have secured a victory

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
to rate something is to judge its worth
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign
the second a, taken as written

explanation.surface: A racehorse is thrown out of a contest after being judged to have won it unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads like disqualifying the horse, but it is the definition: annoyed. GG (gee-gee) is nursery slang for a horse; the captured pair goes in with the V first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is put out is irritated or annoyed, which is the informal sense of aggravated.

clue.text: Popular view, for example

blocks.note: what is popular is in
a stance is a view or position on an issue

explanation.surface: A widely held opinion, offered by way of illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase, not a word: 'for instance' means 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited as an illustration, as in the idiom 'for instance'.

clue.text: Superior American guards took flight

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so these letters enclose others

blocks.note: U is short for upper class, socially superior
US is the United States
to take flight is to run away

explanation.surface: A senior American officer protects someone who has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior American' is two pieces, U and US, which together wrap the middle. The preamble supplies the definition: this is one of the eight planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, one of the eight solutions the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Viewer's complaint occupied middle of last year

indicators.note: what occupies the middle of a phrase sits inside it, so the letters are found within

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a grievance from the middle of last year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' means an eye, not a TV watcher; the answer sits inside 'laST YEar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an ailment of the organ we view with.

clue.text: Old radio stations broadcast over river Rhine, primarily

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are strewn into a new order
primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
the opening letter of the river's name

explanation.surface: Old radio stations were transmitted across the Rhine valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio picture so well it hides its job as the anagram signal. A transistor was the common name for a portable radio in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Transistor was everyday shorthand for the small portable radio that the device made possible, now dated.

clue.text: Girl's set drugs in rows

blocks.note: Di is a short girl's name; with the possessive it becomes Di's
to set something down is to put it
E is ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: A girl arranges her drugs neatly in lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' rhymes with 'cows' here: quarrels, not lines, though the surface wants lines of drugs. E is crossword shorthand for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows in the sense of noisy quarrels are arguments, which is what disputes are.

clue.text: Ace goes back to top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so what is at the back is moved to the front

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a go in a game is a turn, so goes are turns

explanation.surface: A champion player returns to the top of the rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: Join the two pieces, then shift the final letter up to the start. The preamble supplies the definition: this is one of the planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, one of the eight solutions the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Soldier grabs 5 for 23

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: GI Joe is a nickname for an American soldier
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A soldier takes clue 5's answer in place of clue 23's.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-down but is just the number, as a Roman numeral. '23' is a true cross-reference: JUPITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jove is an alternative name for Jupiter, king of the Roman gods, after whom the planet is named.

clue.text: Family members have to run dynamo

blocks.note: in biology a family is made up of genera
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Relatives are expected to keep a lively, energetic person going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family' is the biological rank, not relatives: a family contains several genera.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine that converts mechanical motion into electric current, a kind of generator.

clue.text: Insect maturing and going off at first?

definitions.text: Insect maturing and going off at first?

indicators.note: at first points to the opening of each word, so only the leading letters count

blocks.note: the leading letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An insect grows up and then departs, the question mark hinting at a life cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initials spell the answer, and read straight it describes the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis, which then flies off.

clue.text: Pity about European container train

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: to rue is to regret or pity
E is the abbreviation for European
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A sad comment on a European freight train carrying shipping containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container train' looks like one rail term, but the train here is a royal entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a body of attendants following an important person, which is a retinue.

clue.text: Sister Elizabeth drinks English port

indicators.note: whoever drinks something takes it inside, so these letters swallow others

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
the first letter of the name, the E in ER, Elizabeth Regina
E is the abbreviation for English
Pt is the abbreviation for port in place names

explanation.surface: A nun called Elizabeth enjoys a glass of English port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink, but it is the abbreviation PT in place names such as Pt Moresby. The preamble supplies the definition: a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the eighth and outermost planet from the Sun, one of the preamble's group.

clue.text: Like blood as it enters the ear?

indicators.note: what enters the ear is what is heard, so the spelling follows the sound

blocks.note: venous means relating to veins and the blood in them

explanation.surface: A medical question about how blood behaves when it reaches the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Venous, of the veins, is pronounced like the planet. The preamble supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the second planet from the Sun, one of the eight the preamble groups together.

clue.text: Works in gallery, longing to welcome one school

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: panting for something is longing for it
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: An art gallery hopes to host a group of visiting schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' feels like a school of painters, but it only adds its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings are artworks, and works in a gallery are typically pictures hanging on the walls.

clue.text: Divers here aplenty, when analysed on TV

indicators.note: to analyse is to break something down into parts, so these letters are taken apart and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: TV pundits pick over plenty of footballers who dive to win fouls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' are footballers who fake falls, not swimmers. The penalty box is the area in front of goal where a fall can win a penalty; 'the box' is British slang for TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Players feign fouls chiefly in the penalty area, because a foul there earns a penalty kick.

clue.text: Worked with crook: sped off with deer and two horses

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are spoiled into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A criminal accomplice fled in a getaway with a stag and a pair of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal but is the shepherd's hooked staff. Horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd works with a crook, a hooked staff, to guide a flock, which is shepherding.

clue.text: US pentathlete is getting revised score

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American pentathlete has their competition points recalculated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' sounds like the pentathlete's points, but it is a musical score: Holst's orchestral suite, whose movements are named after planets and explain the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a written musical composition, and Holst's work is a seven-movement orchestral suite.

clue.text: Unhurried one bound to block light

indicators.note: a blockage sits inside a passage, so one piece is lodged within another

blocks.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light
I is the Roman numeral for one
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: A slow-moving person is certain to get in the way of the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests tied up or leaping, but here it means certain, as in 'bound to win'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisured pace is relaxed and slow, with plenty of free time, so it is unhurried.

clue.text: Bother Irish girl not on vacation

indicators.note: a place on vacation has been emptied, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: Ir is the abbreviation for Irish
a girl's name
the word's first and last letters, its middle removed

explanation.surface: An Irish girl is annoyed that she is not going on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bother' reads as a verb but is the noun here: a nuisance. 'On vacation' sounds like a holiday; it means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A bother is a nuisance or source of annoyance, which is exactly what an irritant is.

clue.text: Daughter lives with farmer, a rye producer

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to live is to be, so lives gives is
a tiller tills the soil

explanation.surface: A daughter lives with a farmer who grows rye.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants rye the cereal crop; the definition means rye whiskey, which is distilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is also a whiskey made from rye grain, and whoever makes whiskey is a distiller.

clue.text: Way to start widespread conflict

indicators.note: to start means to come at the beginning, so this piece leads the rest

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
what is rife is widespread

explanation.surface: A recipe for starting a war across a whole region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way to start' reads as 'how to begin', but it is placing the street abbreviation first.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or fighting, so it is a synonym for conflict.

clue.text: Chap recalled collecting 14

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so these letters run backwards
to collect is to gather in, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: a chap is a he
14-across is paintings, which are art

explanation.surface: A man remembers gathering up a cross-referenced item.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 14-across, PAINTINGS, reduced to the general word for them. The preamble supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, our own world, one of the preamble's group of eight.

clue.text: Ten cut disc and show growth

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so this piece slices into the middle of another

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
X is the Roman numeral for ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten people record a disc and display their development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten cut disc' looks like a list, but ten is the Roman numeral sliced into the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to grow larger, so the verb phrase meaning to display growth matches it.

clue.text: Exceptionally huge

blocks.note: surface reading: something enormously big
setter's reading: the odd letters of the second word, exceptional meaning odd, spell a chemical symbol

explanation.walkthrough: Exceptional can mean odd, and the odd letters of 'huge' give HG, the chemical symbol for the metal that shares the planet's name. Ironically, this is the smallest planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is both the innermost planet and the liquid metal whose symbol is Hg, from Latin hydrargyrum.

clue.text: Dams releasing energy

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a dam is a horse's mother, so dams are mares
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Reservoir dams let out water to generate hydroelectric power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dams' looks like barriers holding water; here it is the breeding term for a horse's mother. The preamble supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, the red one, among the eight the preamble groups.

clue.text: Nice setter right to carry up PCs etc

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within, so one piece bears others inside it

blocks.note: in Nice, a French city, the setter would call himself je, French for I
taken as written
IT is information technology, which covers PCs
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pleasant crossword setter is entitled to bring along computers and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not pleasant: the setter there says je, French for I. The preamble supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest, one of the preamble's group of eight.

clue.text: Sport owed money to auditor

indicators.note: an auditor here is a listener, so what counts is how the words come across to the ear

blocks.note: what is owed is due, and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A sportsman is in debt to the accountant checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but it means a hearer. Dough is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art practised as a competitive Olympic sport.

clue.text: Fellow breaks needle and arm

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: to needle someone is to annoy or rile them
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man snaps a needle and injures his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' and 'arm' conjure an injection; one is a verb meaning annoy and the other a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is a weapon, as in firearms, and a rifle is a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: Fiat's big guns touring Italy

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go around it, so these letters encircle another

blocks.note: ordnance is heavy artillery
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Fiat's top executives make a tour of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiat' wants to be the Italian car maker, fitting Italy; it is the noun meaning a decree, and ''s' is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative order or decree, and an ordinance is an official rule or decree.
